questions.text: How many children are in the class?
questions.explanation: There are always 5 children in the class, no matter what.
questions.based_on: There are 5 children in the class.

questions.text: When you put two groups of items together, how do you get the number of things in both groups?
options: the number of things in neither group
the number of things in both groups combined
the number of things in one group
questions.explanation: When you combine two groups, you get the total number of things in both groups.
questions.based_on: When you put two groups of items together, you get the "amount in all" or "total amount".

questions.text: How many sides does a square have?
questions.explanation: A square by definition has 4 sides and 4 vertices.
questions.based_on: A square has 4 sides and 4 vertices.

questions.text: When subtracting two numbers, what must you put the numerals in?
questions.explanation: When you subtract two numbers, the numerals need to be in the correct order.
questions.based_on: When subtracting two numbers, you need to put the numerals in the right place.

questions.text: What is the minimum number of sides a shape must have to be called a triangle?
questions.explanation: A triangle by definition has three sides.
questions.based_on: A shape with 3 sides is a triangle.

questions.text: How many coins are in the bag?
questions.explanation: We know there are 887 coins because we counted them.
questions.based_on: There are 887 coins in the bag.

questions.text: When adding numbers in columns, how do you start adding the numbers?
questions.explanation: You start adding the numbers by adding the units first and then the tens.
questions.based_on: When adding numbers in columns, you add the units first and then the tens.

questions.text: If you have 385 animals and you take away 378, how many animals will you have left?
questions.explanation: If you take away 378 animals from 385, you will be left with 7 animals.
questions.based_on: If you have 385 animals and you take away 378, you will have 7 animals left.

knowledge_base.q: • Manipulate, represent, describe and explore various 2-D shapes • Identify, name, describ
knowledge_base.a: • Manipulate, represent, describe and explore various 2-D shapes • Identify, name, describe and classify 2-D shapes (rectangle, square, circle and triangle) • Draw and manipulate basic 2-D shapes using ICT • Use, read and interpret pictograms • Use ICT to create pictograms representing real-life situations • Recognise, read and write the numbers up to 1 000 in numerals and in words • Count, compare and order numbers up to 1000 • Illustrate the meaning of place value (up to 1000) with and without use of ICT • Recognise and complete patterns in number sequences up to 1000 • Represent 2-digit and 3-digit numbers on an abacus/number house • Use ICT to represent 2-digit/3-digit numbers on an abacus • Perform the two arithmetic operations Addition and Subtraction - Add 2 numbers (up to 3 digits) with and without carrying - Subtract 2 numbers (up to 3 digits) with and without borrowing - Solve one-step routine and non-routine word problem involving the 2 operations (addition;subtraction) • Perform and describe mental calculations involving the 2 operations • Write numbers from 1 to 1000 and perform the 2 arithmetic operations using ICT • Estimate, compare and measure mass (kg/g) • Solve simple word problems involving mass.
